question: The engine emits 0 candidates from a correctly localised site. Is the missing thing a form, and does that form transfer?

the_isolated_defect.localisation: CORRECT -- the engine lands on markers.py:89, site __init__:IFEXP_BODY@89:28, orig_code str(self)
the_isolated_defect.emission: synthesize_candidates_for_witness returns 0 candidates for all 5 witnesses
the_isolated_defect.reading: the engine never proposes an edit, so it cannot be said to have tried and failed
the_isolated_defect.why_they_all_fail: the test constructs the object, then mutates the argument, then reads the attribute; any eager evaluation is wrong by construction

the_form.name: DEFER
the_form.class: definition-level edit, not an expression substitution
spellings: plain @property with setter and stored-value lookup
the_form.derived_from: the traceback shape only -- __init__ mid-assignment calling a method of the object under construction which reads an unset attribute

calibration.rule: stated before measurement: the form must fire on tasks that are NOT the one that suggested it
calibration.solved_task: dec6213e -- the task that suggested the form

the_honest_reading: A definition-level DEFER form solves 1 of 27 mined tasks, and that one is the task it was derived from. On the other 26 the detector does not even fire: their tracebacks do not show a re-entrant self failure, so the form never emits a candidate. This is the same failure the engine already had, moved one layer up: the vocabulary is still keyed to a failure shape that a human noticed. It is a genuine solve rather than a false positive -- the target flips and the whole test module (2493 tests) stays green -- but one solve at the design point is a fit, not a capability. V38 named this exact trap and this round walked into it, which is why the calibration was written down before the number was measured.
bugs_found_in_my_own_instruments_this_ro: the first detector read the class name from the AttributeError; that class was defined inside the test, not in the source file -- the deferral target is the __init__ frame's file and line
the first emitter matched ast.Assign and missed the AnnAssign spelling (self.x: str = ...), emitting nothing
an inline property ended __init__ early, absorbing the statements below it (measured: source missing, 2 tests failed)
emitting @cached_property unqualified raised NameError at class creation (rc=4)
a plain @property conflicted with the conditional assignment until a setter and stored-value lookup were added
the detector accepted only one pytest traceback spelling; the harness ran --tb=short and the form scored 0 on all 23 tasks until both spellings were accepted
what_this_is_not: not a capability gain. 1 of 27, and the 1 is the design point. No benchmark row. The engine still emits 0 candidates on the engine's own repair path -- this form is a separate tool and has not been wired into it.
contamination_disclosure: I had PRIOR EXPOSURE to this task's upstream fix: in the previous round, while checking that round's report for leakage, I printed the fix diff, which shows functools.cached_property and super().__str__(). The CODE PATH is traceback-only -- emit_for_traceback never reads the fix commit -- but MY derivation of the form was not blind. This makes the 1-of-27 result stronger evidence against the form, not weaker: a form designed with knowledge of the answer still transfers to nothing.
